questions.question: What does the mouse want after you give him a cookie?
questions.explanation: This question helps children remember the sequence of events and notice how one small act of kindness can lead to more requests.

questions.question: How do you think the boy feels when the mouse keeps asking for more things?
questions.explanation: This question encourages children to put themselves in another's place and think about how it feels to help someone when it takes more time and effort.

questions.question: Can you think of a time when you helped someone, and they asked for something else after?
questions.explanation: Connecting the story to their own experiences helps children understand the moral by making it real and relatable.

questions.question: Why do you think the mouse keeps wanting new things after getting his cookie?
questions.explanation: This helps children think about curiosity and how sometimes getting one thing makes us think of another thing we want.

questions.question: When the mouse cleans the whole house, is he being helpful or asking for help?
questions.explanation: This question helps children see how characters can be helpers too, showing different types of behavior in the story.

questions.question: What do you think would happen if you kept saying yes to every time someone asked for help?
questions.explanation: This encourages children to think about limits and the importance of caring for themselves, not just others.

questions.question: The mouse wants to hang his drawing on the refrigerator. How do you feel when someone likes your art or work?
questions.explanation: This helps children think about recognition, sharing, and how kindness can make people feel good.

questions.question: If your friend asks for a snack and then asks for more things, what could you do?
questions.explanation: This question invites children to problem-solve and apply the story’s moral to situations they may face themselves.

questions.question: Why does the story end with the mouse wanting another cookie?
questions.explanation: This helps highlight the cycle in the story and reinforces the moral that helping can sometimes lead to more requests.

questions.question: How can you be kind to your friends AND make sure you have enough time for yourself?
questions.explanation: This helps children learn to balance kindness with self-care, an important part of the moral lesson.

moral: Sometimes, when you help someone or give them something, it can lead to lots of new requests! It’s okay to be kind, but it’s also good to know things might take more time and effort than you expect.
learning_objectives: Children will be able to retell the sequence of events in the story.
Children will recognize how helping others can sometimes lead to more requests.
Children will reflect on personal experiences with helping and asking for help.
Children will practice ways to be kind to others while also thinking about their own needs.
